Sunbound Acquires Richter Healthcare Consultants And Raises $24 Million Series A
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Sunbound Acquires Richter Healthcare Consultants And Raises $24 Million Series A
Sunbound has acquired Richter Healthcare Consultants, combining its AI-powered revenue operating system for senior living with Richter’s more than 25 years of experience in revenue cycle management, accounting, Medicaid eligibility, reimbursement, and consulting for post-acute and senior care providers.
The acquisition follows Sunbound’s $24 million Series A funding round led by TTV Capital, with participation from Bling Capital, Fika Ventures, Live Oak Bank, and Ziegler Linkage Fund. The financing brings Sunbound’s total funding to $36 million and will support business expansion and continued product development.
Richter serves skilled nursing, senior living, home health, and hospice operators nationwide. Its services span outsourced revenue cycle management, accounting and controller services, Medicaid eligibility, reimbursement and clinical consulting, audit and compliance support, and EHR implementation and optimization.
Jennifer Richter, CPA, Founder and CEO of Richter, will remain with the combined company in a new role focused on industry partnerships and product strategy. Sunbound said customers of both companies will continue receiving uninterrupted service while gaining access to the combined platform’s broader capabilities over time.
The transaction also expands Sunbound further into skilled nursing, where billing and reimbursement workflows can be particularly complex. Together, Sunbound and Richter are on track to process approximately $3 billion in annualized payment volume.
Sunbound’s platform is designed to manage the revenue cycle from admission through payment. Its technology covers admissions, private payments, end-to-end revenue cycle management, and working capital, while combining automation with human revenue specialists who manage exceptions and more complex financial workflows.
The company said operators using its claims platform achieve a 99% claims collection rate and 96% first-pass acceptance rate. Sunbound also claims its private payments tools can save more than 40 hours per community each month by moving families toward digital payments and automating collections-related workflows.
Its admissions product is designed to verify payer coverage and a prospective resident’s ability to pay in approximately 30 seconds before a bed is committed. By combining those capabilities with Richter’s clinical, financial, and operational expertise, Sunbound plans to offer senior care providers a more comprehensive alternative to using multiple vendors for revenue and financial operations.
TTV Capital said the investment reflects growing demand for modern financial technology across senior living and skilled nursing. Sunbound is also backed by industry investors including Omega Healthcare Investors and Live Oak Ventures.

Our platform directly addresses the operational inefficiencies, financial underperformance, and cash flow issues that have plagued operators for years. articles.text:
Acta Pharmaceuticals Raises $24 Million Seed To Advance Alzheimer’s Disease Early Intervention Pipeline
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
Acta Pharmaceuticals Raises $24 Million Seed To Advance Alzheimer’s Disease Early Intervention Pipeline
Acta Pharmaceuticals has raised $24 million in total seed financing to advance a pipeline of therapies designed for earlier intervention in Alzheimer’s disease, including its lead gamma-secretase modulator, GSM-779690T.
The Boston-based company was created to translate more than four decades of Alzheimer’s research from scientific founder Dr. Rudolph E. Tanzi into potential new therapies. Its lead program is the result of approximately 25 years of gamma-secretase modulator research conducted by Tanzi and the late Dr. Steven L. Wagner at Massachusetts General Hospital and the University of California, San Diego.
GSM-779690T is being developed as a once-daily oral small-molecule treatment intended for early-stage, long-duration disease modification and potentially prevention. The drug is designed to lower levels of Aβ42, an amyloid-beta protein associated with plaque formation, while increasing Aβ37 and Aβ38, which can interfere with aggregation. Unlike earlier gamma-secretase inhibitors, the approach selectively modulates the enzyme while seeking to preserve its normal biological functions.
Acta is evaluating GSM-779690T in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study in healthy adult volunteers. The trial is designed to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics across single and multiple ascending doses. Preclinical studies cited by the company showed single-digit nanomolar potency against Aβ42, a near 1:1 brain-to-plasma ratio in mice, and oral bioavailability across multiple species.
Beyond its lead program, Acta is developing combination therapies based on research using Alzheimer’s-in-a-Dish, a laboratory platform developed by Tanzi and Massachusetts General Hospital colleagues. The models recreate important features of Alzheimer’s pathology and the aging brain and allow researchers to screen large numbers of approved drugs and natural compounds. The research has identified more than 30 validated combinations that the company said can curb Alzheimer’s pathology, with Acta licensing related intellectual property from MGH and advancing selected candidates toward clinical evaluation.
Tanzi’s research has played a significant role in the scientific understanding of Alzheimer’s disease. He co-discovered the familial Alzheimer’s genes APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 and has authored more than 800 scientific papers and holds approximately 50 patents. He is Director of the Genetics and Aging Research Unit and the McCance Center for Brain Health at Massachusetts General Hospital and serves as Joseph P. and Rose F. Kennedy Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School.
Acta said approximately $70 million in preclinical development funding supported the research that ultimately led to GSM-779690T. The company’s shareholders include Alzheimer’s Disease Research Foundation, Dolby Family Ventures, Gamma Bio Investors, family offices, and other mission-driven investors.
The new financing will support Acta as it moves its lead program through clinical development while expanding a broader pipeline aimed at intervening earlier in the Alzheimer’s disease process. GSM-779690T remains investigational and has not been approved by any regulatory authority.

articles.text:
University of Pennsylvania Receives $22.5 Million Gift From Gabriel And Stephanie Gilinski
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
University of Pennsylvania Receives $22.5 Million Gift From Gabriel And Stephanie Gilinski
The University of Pennsylvania has received a $22.5 million gift from Gabriel Gilinski and Stephanie Gilinski to expand financial aid and establish endowed faculty positions within Penn Arts & Sciences.
The gift will establish the Gabriel Gilinski and Stephanie Gilinski Endowed Scholarship for undergraduate students in the College of Arts & Sciences, including students coming to Penn from Latin America.
It will also establish two endowed professorships spanning Penn’s history, political science and economics departments.
A visiting professorship will also be created to bring distinguished scholars to Penn for teaching, research and academic collaboration.
The scholarship expands Penn’s broader affordability initiatives, including its Quaker Commitment to meet demonstrated undergraduate financial need with grant-based, no-loan financial aid.
Gabriel Gilinski graduated from Penn in 2008 with a political science degree and a minor in economics.
He currently chairs Grupo Nutresa, a Latin American food company with more than 50,000 employees, 45 factories and operations spanning 17 countries.
The company’s philanthropic arm, Fundación Nutresa, supports educational scholarships as well as healthcare and nutrition programs.
KEY QUOTES:
“Penn is at its best when we bring talented students together with outstanding faculty and give them the opportunity to learn from one another. Gabriel and Stephanie’s generous commitment expands access to a Penn education while investing in the scholars whose outstanding teaching and research enrich our academic community. We are deeply grateful for their partnership.”
J. Larry Jameson, President of the University of Pennsylvania
“On behalf of the School of Arts & Sciences, I am delighted to express our profound gratitude to Gabriel and Stephanie Gilinski. Arts & Sciences is built upon the eminence of our faculty, who pursue the highest standards in their fields while unlocking the brilliance and potential of future generations. It is also shaped by international students and scholars, who bring their unique approaches to bear on some of the most pressing issues of our time. The Gilinskis’ generosity will have a profound impact, not just for individual students and scholars, but for the entire Penn community.”
Mark Trodden, Dean of the School of Arts & Sciences and Thomas S. Gates, Jr. Professor of Physics & Astronomy
“I’m a firm believer in the importance of the liberal arts and in the value of the critical thinking skills I developed through my studies in the College. Exceptional faculty are at the heart of Penn’s mission, and we are proud to support the recruitment and retention of scholars who bring complex problems to life in the classroom, make groundbreaking discoveries in their research, and provide students with unique opportunities to discover and learn.”

Co-led by Long Journey Ventures and Abstract Ventures, the round follows a January launch and rapid growth that now has OuterSignal powering thousands of consumer businesses and hundreds of millions of orders.
NEW YORK , Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OuterSignal , the agentic customer intelligence platform that tells brands who their customers actually are and activates them 1:1, today announced a $22M Series A co-led by Long Journey Ventures and Abstract Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Top Shelf Ventures, SuperAngel.Fund , and Jerry Yang's AME Cloud Ventures. As angels, participation included Dave Heath , Rohan Shah, Alex Haro , Emery Wells, Kim Perell , Michael Preysman , Michael Perry, Ken Nguyen , Raad Mobrem , Zach Sims , Sahil Bloom, Steve Carroll, Michael Loeb , Rich Vogel, Troy Ossinoff , Sahil Bhaiwala , James Beshara and Nik Sharma, along with dozens of executives from OuterSignal's customer base.
Every day, hundreds of millions of consumers are treated like strangers. The gym buff, the new mom and the retiree get the same email, see the same products and load the same homepage because brands know almost nothing about who they are. OuterSignal transforms that, using public context to build a full picture of the person behind the purchase. From there, OuterSignal's agents put that to work.
That changes the work of nearly every team:
Influencer and partnerships teams learn when a notable customer buys and can reach out while it matters.
Lifecycle marketers build audiences around real personas, so college students and busy executives each get bespoke flows and campaigns written for them.
Acquisition teams send precise segments to media platforms and run ads that speak to the people who actually buy.
Product and merchandising teams see who is behind every SKU and category they manage.
OuterSignal customers report measurable lift across retention, acquisition, conversion and influencer marketing. Brands on the platform include AG1, HexClad, Jones Road Beauty, True Classic, Jomashop, Lucy, Gratsi, Magic Mind, and thousands more.
"We built OuterSignal to solve the very problem I had running consumer businesses over the last 15 years," said Zach Zelner, co-founder and CEO of OuterSignal. "Generative AI finally makes truly 1:1 experiences possible, but only if you understand each person on the other end. This round allows us to continue building best-in-class intelligence that drives person-level personalization across billions of touchpoints."
"OuterSignal's platform unlocks a new paradigm for agentic personalization. Their growth has been remarkable and we're proud to back them as they power delightful marketing and experiences for all consumer businesses," said Ramtin Naimi, Founder & General Partner, Abstract Ventures.
"OuterSignal is building something no consumer brand will want to run without. Technology like this is rare, and so is a company that moves this fast. We're thrilled to partner with them," said Lee Jacobs, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Long Journey Ventures.

articles.text:
University Of Washington-Led Optoelectronics Center Receives $22 Million NSF Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
University Of Washington-Led Optoelectronics Center Receives $22 Million NSF Award
The University of Washington-led Center for Integration of Modern Optoelectronic Materials on Demand is expected to receive $22 million from the U.S. National Science Foundation over the next five years to continue research involving advanced optoelectronics and semiconductor materials.
Known as NSF IMOD, the center brings together researchers from 14 universities across the U.S.
It was originally established in 2021 as an NSF Science and Technology Center.
The new funding represents a second five-year period of support for the center.
NSF IMOD combines research across chemistry, physics, engineering, and materials science to develop materials capable of integrating light and electronics.
Potential applications include photorealistic virtual reality displays, quantum communications, semiconductor technology, and future photonic computing systems.
One major research focus involves quantum dots.
The center’s researchers have developed techniques for printing quantum dots and positioning them within specific cavities that could eventually be used in quantum communications and quantum computing systems.
The team intends to further develop the quantum dots and supporting structures during the next five years.
NSF IMOD also runs extensive education and workforce development programs.
Graduate students participate in interdisciplinary training spanning chemical synthesis, quantum mechanics, materials science, and advanced semiconductor technologies.
Students also gain industry experience through internships with companies and national laboratories.
Partners include UbiQD, Nanopattern Technologies, FOM Technologies, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Tandem PV, and Nanosys-Shoei Chemical.
During its first five years, NSF IMOD researchers published 140 papers, hosted 36 undergraduate students through its Research Experience for Undergraduates program, and conducted more than 85 outreach events.
The 14 participating institutions include the University of Washington, UC Berkeley, Columbia University, University of Chicago, Northwestern University, University of Pennsylvania, University of Maryland, Georgia Tech, University of Colorado Boulder, Arizona State University, Rice University, Lehigh University, City College of New York, and University of Maryland, Baltimore County.
KEY QUOTES:
“The point of this center is to tackle problems that are too big for one scientist or even two or three to tackle by themselves.”
David Ginger, Director of NSF IMOD and Professor of Chemistry at the University of Washington
“We’re really excited to see our students start taking important roles, and then eventually we hope they move into leadership roles in this space of commercializing new semiconductor materials.”
David Ginger, Director of NSF IMOD and Professor of Chemistry at the University of Washington
“Just as the atomic structure of a quantum dot produces unique and exciting properties, the exceptionally interdisciplinary structure of NSF IMOD is enabling foundational science and technological innovations that would not otherwise be possible.”
Birgit Schwenzer, Program Director in the NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences
